sections.title: 500 Years of Architecture in Philadelphia
sections.description:
Philadelphia has a deep built environment history that spans many centuries. The fertile
peninsula between the Delaware and the Schuylkill rivers shows traces of human
occupation for the last 12,000 years. The course will depart from those archaeological sites
and the names they lent us: Passyunk, Manayunk, Tulpehocken, Wissahickon, in order to
develop a basis upon which to understand what we built after: the European settlement
founded by William Penn in 1682. From there we will explore the colonial architecture, the
19th century expansion around commerce and industry and the many canonical structures
built here in the 20th and 21stcenturies.
The course is organized around 8 units, each one a pair of site visits and seminar
discussions.
Co-taught by Fernando Lara, Professor of Architecture and William Whitaker, Director of
the Architectural Archives, this seminar is a unique opportunity for our cosmopolitan
student body to learn about the rich history of architecture in the place they call home
while studying at Penn.
